title: Evo: a foundation model for DNA, from molecules to genomes
summary: Published in Science, Evo (Arc Institute, Stanford, and UC Berkeley) designed EvoCas9-1, a CRISPR system sharing only about 73% of its sequence with CRISPR-Cas9 but with comparable activity after eleven designs, and new IS200/IS605 transposons that cut and paste DNA. The team calls this the beginning and conducted an ethics and safety study.
organization: Arc Institute; Stanford, and UC Berkeley

evidence.tested: Evo was prompted to generate CRISPR systems; EvoCas9-1 was obtained after testing eleven designs, validated in the lab by an experimental biology subteam.
evidence.unknown: The page gives no success rates or error analysis, and an ethics and safety investigation addressed potential risks rather than efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: Evo, a DNA-trained foundation model, designed the protein and RNA components of EvoCas9-1 and new IS200/IS605 transposons.
